title: Registers and marks
goal: Keep several pieces of text at hand without losing them, and jump back to places you've been.

lessons.title: Named registers and the yank register

concepts.desc: yank into / put from register a (any of a-z).
uppercase name: APPEND to register a instead of overwriting it.
the yank register: holds your last yank, even after you delete things.
the last nine deleted lines; each new line delete shifts them down.
the unnamed register used by plain y, d, c, p.
show register contents.

lessons.tip: Classic trap: yank a word, delete the text to replace, press p, and you get the deleted text back. Use "0p. Your config uses clipboard=unnamedplus, so plain y/p go through the system clipboard; named registers always behave the same.

quiz.q: You yanked a line, then deleted another one. How do you paste the yanked line?
Yank the current line into register q.
Add the current line to what's already in register q.
How do you see what's in all registers?
What's in register "1?
quiz.a: The most recently deleted (or changed) line(s); older ones shift to "2-"9.

quiz.q: Put register b above the cursor line.

lessons.title: Special registers and Ctrl-r

concepts.desc: black hole register: delete without overwriting any register.
system clipboard / primary selection (needs a clipboard provider; in WSL install win32yank).
in insert or command-line mode: insert a register's contents.
expression register: type math or a Vim expression, Enter inserts the result.
last inserted text / last command / current file name / last search.
on the command line: insert the word under the cursor.

lessons.tip: Ctrl-r is the fastest way to reuse text while typing: Ctrl-r 0 pastes your yank, Ctrl-r / your last search, Ctrl-r = does sums.

quiz.q: Delete a line without touching any register.
In insert mode, paste the contents of register a.
Insert the result of 24*7 while typing.
Which register holds the current file name?
Yank the current line to the system clipboard.
While typing a :s command, how do you insert the word under the cursor?

lessons.title: Marks

concepts.desc: set a mark in this file.
jump to the line of mark a / its exact position.
marks are motions: delete to the mark line, yank to the exact mark.
uppercase marks are global: 'A opens the file and jumps there.
back to where you were before the last jump.
list the marks.

lessons.tip: Set a mark before you go elsewhere to look something up (ma), then come back with `a. For a one-off, `` (back to before the jump) needs no mark.

quiz.q: Set mark x here, and later jump to its exact column.
Delete everything from the current line up to the line with mark a.
What's special about mark `B` (uppercase)?
quiz.a: It's global: it remembers the file too, so 'B jumps across files.

quiz.q: Difference between 'a and `a?
quiz.a: 'a goes to the first non-blank of the mark's line; `a goes to the exact line and column.

quiz.q: Return to where you were before your last G or search jump.
List all marks.

lessons.title: Jump list and change list

concepts.desc: back / forward through the jump list (G, gg, /search, %, marks... are jumps). Works across files.
back / forward through the places you changed text.
jump to the last change.
start / end of the last changed or yanked text (e.g. what you just pasted).
back into insert mode where you last left it.
show the lists.

lessons.tip: Ctrl-o is your back button. After jumping to a definition or a search result, Ctrl-o brings you back, even into the previous file.

quiz.q: You searched and jumped away. How do you go back to where you were?
Jump to where you last changed text.
Difference between Ctrl-o and g;?
quiz.a: Ctrl-o walks the jump list (places you jumped from); g; walks the change list (places you edited).

quiz.q: Select exactly the text you just pasted.
Is j a jump that Ctrl-o returns from?
quiz.a: No. Only jump motions (G, gg, /, n, %, marks, etc.) go in the jump list.

quiz.q: Move forward again after pressing Ctrl-o too often.
